findings.summary: A rewrite could still produce a page that MatchesPage no longer matches, if the memory's type or revision value ends in `---`. The input guard in shapeOf checks only the original block, not the block that rewrittenIdentity builds.
evidence: rewrittenIdentity writes `source_type: <m.Type>` through writeField (frontmatter.go:209, `%s: %s\n`) with no check on the value.
If m.Type from memorycard ends in `---`, the new line ends in `---\n`. frontmatterBlock (address.go:81-87, SplitN on `---\n`) would then close the block at that line.
MatchesPage would then see a different frontmatter hash than the one recorded as hashText(newBlock). The page would read as hand-edited on the next run.

I did not run this and did not check whether memorycard can hold such a type. Pre-existing behavior of the rewrite; this commit did not introduce it. A cheap fix is to re-run the shapeOf agreement check on newBlock+body before planning.
Read all of longterm-mem/internal/promote/migrate_cards.go in the worktree. Read frontmatterBlock (address.go:81-88) and writeField (frontmatter.go:209).

Uncounted legacy pages: a page whose first non-blank line is `---` and that is not readable falls into the unreadable scan. That scan trims BOM, blank lines, spaces, tabs and `\r`, and stops at the first closing rule, ignoring trailing spaces and tabs. I found no `---`-opening page that escapes the legacy-key count.

Unreadable pages never reach backup or write. legacyPagesOf sets block to "" for them. MigrateCardPages refuses them with RefusedUnreadable (lines 348-351) before mapPage and before plan append. applyMigration backs up only the addresses in plan.

Shared code: shapeOf is only called from legacyPagesOf. I did not run `git diff`, so I did not confirm that address.go and MatchesPage are unchanged. The functions I read looked untouched and are only called, not edited.
